platform: macOS 26.5 (25F71), arm64, Apple Silicon; debug build 3196ce2 with embedded frontend, WKWebView through the test bridge (src-tauri/src/test_bridge.rs)
isolation: own data folder and WKWebView store (test-instance.mjs); default stores unchanged at the end; nothing typed reaches a shell or the engine (send_input refused by the harness IPC guard, the pending message discarded)
method: Three inputs appended to the app page (plain, spellcheck=false, spellcheck=false + autocorrect/autocapitalize off), then the app's own composers: the welcome screen's 'Your first message' field (EmptySessionScreen) and, after a conversation is started with a refused first message, the conversation's 'Message Muse' field (Composer). The same text is inserted one character at a time (as typing delivers it) and as one insertion, through Input.insertText (AppKit insertText:), and read back. System text-substitution settings left at the macOS defaults (NSAutomaticQuoteSubstitutionEnabled and NSAutomaticDashSubstitutionEnabled not set). Replay on 3196ce2 (spellCheck={false} on the terminal input and both composers): the composers are now expected to keep straight quotes and '--'; the plain probe input still substitutes (the system default, kept as the control).
limits: The terminal field itself is measured in m1-05-terminal-macos*.json, check typed-quotes.
Input.insertText through the bridge, not a physical keyboard.

previousRun.observed: probe inputs only: a plain input turned `echo 'a b' "c d" -- x` typed per character into `echo ‘a b’ “c d” — x`; spellcheck=false kept it. The composers had no spellcheck attribute then and were not measured.
